webcdoc reads a `.webc` file and writes one JSON record describing the component: props, slots, CSS custom properties, parts, events, examples, and the page data and helpers the template reaches for. The docs live in WebC's own server-only comments, so nothing ships to the page, and a component with no comments at all still yields a usable record.

## Packages

| Package | Role |
| --- | --- |
| [`@allons-y/webcdoc-schema`](packages/webcdoc-schema) | TypeScript types and the JSON Schema for the record and the grouped document |
| [`@allons-y/webcdoc`](packages/webcdoc) | The parser, the `webcdoc` CLI, and a Custom Elements Manifest adapter |
| [`@allons-y/webcdoc-tools`](packages/webcdoc-tools) | Pure helpers for filtering, looking up, and ordering the components in a webcdoc document |
| [`@allons-y/webcdoc-lint`](packages/webcdoc-lint) | Validates a webcdoc document against its JSON Schema and lints its components |
| [`@allons-y/cem-plugin-webc`](plugins/cem-plugin-webc) | A Custom Elements Manifest analyzer plugin that reads `.webc` files; opt-in for projects already running the analyzer |

The documentation site lives in [`site`](site) and is not published.

## Quick start

```sh
yarn add --dev @allons-y/webcdoc
yarn webcdoc "components/**/*.webc" --out webcdoc.json
```

Each package README covers its install, usage, and options.

## Development

```sh
corepack enable
yarn install
yarn ci      # build every workspace and render the site
yarn lint    # opx lint
yarn test    # vitest, every workspace
```

Node 24 and Yarn 4 (via Corepack). Releases use [changesets](https://github.com/changesets/changesets): add one with `yarn changeset` for any change a consumer would notice.
